subject: general
question: Which of the following departments released the 2025 Economic Survey of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Department of Economic Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Department of Economic Affairs** is a part of the **Ministry of Finance**, Government of India, and is primarily responsible for the preparation and release of the **Economic Survey of India**, including the **2025 edition**.
 
• The **Economic Survey** provides a detailed analysis of the country’s economic progress, challenges, and outlook for the coming financial year, serving as a precursor to the Union Budget.
 
• The Survey is typically released a day before the presentation of the Union Budget in **Parliament**. It is a crucial document for policymakers, economists, and researchers.
 
• The Department of Economic Affairs works closely with the **Chief Economic Advisor (CEA)** to compile and prepare this document. The CEA plays a pivotal role in shaping its content and focus.
 
• The Survey addresses various aspects, such as **economic growth rates, fiscal policy, monetary policy, inflation trends, external sector performance, and employment statistics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Survey of India:**

 
 
• The **Economic Survey** is an annual document that reviews the performance of the Indian economy over the past year and presents policy recommendations for the upcoming year.
 
• The first Economic Survey of India was published in **1950-51** and was initially included in the Union Budget documents. It became a standalone document from **1964**.
 
• It is regarded as the government’s flagship economic report and is prepared under the guidance of the **Chief Economic Advisor (CEA)**.
 
• The Survey is divided into two volumes: **Volume I** focuses on conceptual and analytical issues, while **Volume II** provides detailed statistical data and sectoral analysis.
 
 
 
• **Department of Economic Affairs (DEA):**
 
 
• The DEA is one of the five departments under the **Ministry of Finance**. It is responsible for handling the economic policy framework and financial regulations in India.
 
• Its functions include managing the **country’s external debt, currency exchange policies, and financial market regulations**.
 
• The department oversees the preparation of crucial financial documents, such as the **Union Budget, Economic Survey, and various fiscal reports**.
 
• It also collaborates with international organizations like the **IMF, World Bank, and Asian Development Bank** on financial and economic matters.
 
 
 
• **Chief Economic Advisor (CEA):**
 
 
• The CEA is the principal advisor to the government on economic matters and plays a vital role in preparing the **Economic Survey**.
 
• The position is typically held by an eminent economist with expertise in macroeconomic policy and research.
 
• The CEA provides inputs on issues such as **GDP growth, inflation, fiscal deficit, and structural reforms**.
 
• The tenure of the CEA is generally for **three years**, and the individual reports directly to the **Finance Minister**.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget vs. Economic Survey:**
 
 
• The **Union Budget** is a financial statement that outlines the government’s revenue and expenditure for the upcoming fiscal year. It is presented in **February** each year.
 
• The **Economic Survey**, on the other hand, is a review of the economy’s performance in the past year and includes policy suggestions to address current challenges.
 
• While the Budget is focused on fiscal planning, the Survey emphasizes broader economic trends and strategic recommendations.
 
• Both documents are critical for understanding the economic priorities and direction of the government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Economic Survey** acts as a tool for initiating public discussions on economic policy and reform measures.
 
• It provides insights into topics like **climate change, digital economy, healthcare, education, and employment**.
 
• Recent editions have highlighted the importance of **Aatmanirbhar Bharat, green energy transition, and post-pandemic recovery**.
 
• India’s GDP growth rate projections and fiscal deficit targets are key features of the Survey that garner widespread attention.
 
• The Survey also includes innovative chapters, such as those on behavioral economics and data-driven governance, to address emerging challenges.
